newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Air Mauritius boss to join Air Afrique next year.
newsitem.headline: Air Mauritius boss to join Air Afrique next year.

text.p: Air Mauritius chairman and managing director, Sir Harry Tirvengadum, said on Thursday he will join Air Afrique in 1997 with a diagnosis of the debt-plagued multinational carrier's problems his top priority.

"After going there, I will carry out a diagnosis before deciding what to do. I received the job offer a little more than 48 hours ago and I cannot put up a realist plan right now," Tirvengadum told Reuters by telephone.
He declined to give a precise date on when he would join Air Afrique because of prior engagements in the travel industry at the local and regional levels.
"I am presently working on a plan to disengage myself from these commitments. But it's definitely going to be next year."
Tirvengadum was chosen as chief of Air Afrique last Monday during a meeting of heads of state and other government representatives of the airline's owners in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan.
He will replace Frenchman Yves-Roland Billecart, whose job as chairman and managing director will be split, with a chairman to be chosen at the next meeting of the company's board.

Tirvengadum said privatisation of Air Afrique would be a longer-term aim. "Ultimately, it must be done. But this will come in the longer run as the airline will first have to be put back on its feet," he said, without setting any target date.

Air Afrique, set up in 1961, is majority owned by Benin, Burkina Faso, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, Ivory Coast, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Senegal and Togo. Air France and other third parties also have a stake.
